policy_presence.summary: Johns Hopkins distributes AI policy governance across IT responsible-use and data governance rules, Teaching @ JHU and CTEI guidance, Whiting Engineering for Professionals (EP) course color categorizations, and graduate misconduct procedures.

coursework.summary: Engineering for Professionals (EP) implements a course-level color classification system for generative AI use: Red (GenAI is prohibited, including drafting, editing and revision, unless the instructor or applicable course instructions explicitly state otherwise), Yellow (moderate AI permitted with restrictions and required disclosure), and Green (liberal AI permitted with transparency). Course-level designation is mandatory; Yellow courses must also include assignment-level labels. This policy applies strictly to EP courses and does not establish a blanket university-wide permission.

exams.summary: In Engineering for Professionals (EP) courses, assessments designated Red prohibit generative AI assistance, including drafting, editing and revision, unless the instructor or applicable course instructions explicitly state otherwise. Students must follow specific course and examination instructions; tool access does not confer examination permission, and unauthorized AI use is subject to disciplinary procedures.

ai_disclosure.summary: In Yellow and Green EP courses, students must adhere to instructor standards for AI disclosure, where full transcripts, model/site citations, or visual highlighting serve as potential examples. Students must save AI outputs and interaction records if disclosure or verification is requested by the course. Hopkins Press requires authors to disclose generative AI use in submissions and will not credit AI as an author.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Johns Hopkins IT policies prohibit entering non-public proprietary Hopkins data (including clinical, financial, and business records) into unapproved third-party AI tools. Meeting hosts should not enable Zoom AI Companion features for meetings involving student education records (FERPA recommendation). HopGPT is approved for sensitive data including PHI and PII, subject to institutional stewardship and required research approvals (IRB for non-clinical research; SIP for clinical research or uses involving PHI/PII).

academic_integrity.summary: Under Graduate Academic Misconduct Procedures applying to KSAS and WSE (Homewood 2017 / AAP 2018), informal resolution of first offenses requires AIO consultation, sanction not exceeding course failure, and mutual agreement reported to the AIO. Hearing Panels apply the preponderance-of-the-evidence standard. Except for informal first-offense resolutions, appeals must be submitted in writing to the AIO or designee for the Cognizant Dean within 10 university business days of the date of the outcome notice, limited to material procedural error, new unavailable information, or excessive sanction. Appeals involve a file review rather than another hearing. CTEI detector guidance is instructional advice rather than a university-wide ban.

approved_tools.summary: Johns Hopkins provides ChatGPT Edu ($8.50/mo base plus usage for full-time faculty/staff), HopGPT (secure internal LLM), Copilot Web (free, non-HIPAA), Microsoft 365 Copilot ($215/yr, HIPAA-compliant), Claude ($22/$55 recharge for active affiliates 18+ on campus or VPN), and Zoom AI Companion (hosts should not enable for FERPA student records). Institutional tool access does not confer coursework or exam authorization.

named_ai_services.summary: Johns Hopkins provides ChatGPT Edu ($8.50/mo base plus usage for full-time faculty/staff), HopGPT (secure internal LLM), Copilot Web (free, non-HIPAA), Microsoft 365 Copilot ($215/yr, HIPAA-compliant), Claude ($22/$55 recharge for active affiliates 18+ on campus or VPN), and Zoom AI Companion (hosts should not enable for FERPA student records). Institutional tool access does not confer coursework or exam authorization.

teaching_guidance.summary: Teaching @ JHU and CTEI provide recommendations for faculty on instructional uses of generative AI, divisional policy consultation, accessibility considerations, and cautious evaluation of AI detection software.

research_guidance.summary: Hopkins Press policy requires authors to disclose generative AI use in publisher submissions; manuscripts substantially written by AI are not accepted. Research use of HopGPT requires IRB approval for non-clinical research and SIP approval for clinical research or uses involving PHI/PII.

security_procurement.summary: Johns Hopkins IT enforces strict prohibitions against sharing non-public proprietary Hopkins data with unapproved third-party AI tools. Approved enterprise tools include HopGPT (with IRB/SIP compliance) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (HIPAA-compliant).
